scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: I'm covering the monitoring desk today and part of
the network has gone missing from the screens after one of the boxes was
restarted. The senior people are clear about what happened: the two parts
were joined by something called a "virtual link", and traffic trying to cross
it now just disappears. I won't pretend I know what a virtual link is -- that
is your area, not mine. What I can see is that the far part is unreachable,
and it went missing right after that restart, so this is on your side. Check
how the two parts are joined and reconnect them today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: The OSPF virtual link (VL) between r4 (Router-ID 14.1.4.1) and r8 (Router-ID 18.1.4.1), transiting Area 1, is the mechanism joining Area 2 (r8's loopbacks and stub segment BB) to the backbone. After r8 was restarted, the VL re-formed and reached Full adjacency status — so the control plane looks healthy — but the post-restart database synchronisation over the VL silently failed to deliver one critical LSA to r8: the Type 4 ASBR Summary LSA (Link State ID 112.1.1.1, Advertising Router 111.1.1.1=r1, Metric 10) that r1 generates to advertise the location of ASBR r11 (Router-ID 112.1.1.1). Every other backbone router (r1, r3, r4, r9) carries this LSA in their Area 0 LSDB; r8's Area 0 LSDB shows exactly 72 LSAs versus the 73 everyone else holds, and its ASBR-summary section is completely empty. Without that Type 4 LSA, r8 cannot compute a path to the ASBR, so — despite possessing all 11 Type 5 AS-external LSAs (redistributed from EIGRP by r11) — it installs zero external routes. Confirmed: ping from r8 to 102.1.1.1 and 120.1.1.1 returns "Network is unreachable", while backbone router r3 reaches those same addresses with 0% loss. The OSPF intra- and inter-area routes on r8 are unaffected (r8 can reach backbone loopbacks and r11's OSPF-domain interface 111.1.1.2 normally). Root cause: after r8's restart the VL database-exchange did not propagate the pre-existing Type 4 ASBR Summary LSA from r4 to r8, leaving Area 2 blind to all AS-external destinations. Corrective fix: on r8, execute `vtysh -c "clear ip ospf process"` to tear down and rebuild the VL adjacency; the fresh Exchange/Loading cycle will re-deliver the missing Type 4 LSA, after which r8's SPF will install the external routes and connectivity will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: Agent notes the r4<->r8 virtual-link is up but does not state that PC0 can reach PC12 end-to-end, so it fails to record the required baseline reachability.

The agent collected useful evidence (VL adjacency up, OSPF/route outputs, successful pings to r8 from other routers) but the writeup asserts specific missing Type-4 LSAs and r8 dataplane failures (pings from r8 to externals, zero external routes) without explicit log entries proving those claims. The reasoning contains plausible inferences but omits key corroborating checks (r8 LSDB dump, r8 route table showing missing externals, direct pings from r8), so the conclusion is under-supported.
